snippet.title: Hilfe, meine Solaranlage stört! – Teil 2: HF-Zange selbst bauen  ⚠️

snippet.title: Everything You Were Told About Taqiyya is WRONG!
snippet.description:
Learn what is taqiyya and how it functions as a concept of self-protection during persecution in Islamic theology. Clarify common misconceptions surrounding this term today.

This breakdown explores the specific meaning of taqiyya within Islamic law. Many misunderstand this concept as a general license to deceive, but this video clarifies that taqiyya is strictly reserved for situations involving immediate danger or severe persecution. It is not a broad permission for Muslims to lie to non-Muslims, as honesty remains a fundamental requirement in the faith.

We analyze the conditions under which this practice is applicable and why it ceases once the threat passes. If you are interested in accurate definitions of Islamic concepts, this overview provides the necessary context to understand the religious boundaries regarding truth and safety. By examining the theological evidence, viewers gain a clearer perspective on how scholars define the limits of this practice.

In June the Treasury issued General License X. It let Iranian crude be produced, sold, shipped, insured and paid for in dollars, and it carried a printed expiry of Friday, August 21, 2026. That printed date is the only place the countdown ever came from.

On July 7 OFAC revoked it and replaced it with General License X1, a ten day wind down for business already underway. X1 closed on July 17. Nothing has replaced it since. As of the August 19 broadcast that was 43 days with no authorization for Iranian oil transactions.

So Friday is the expiration date on a piece of paper that stopped working in July.

Here is why it got past everyone, islander. The June issuance was covered by every outlet on earth, because sanctions relief is a headline. The July revocation ran almost entirely in law firm memos. Norton Rose Fulbright had it. Baker McKenzie had it. Foley had it. The National Law Review had it. A revocation is a memo, and memos do not trend.

Sources: OFAC recent actions 20260622_33 and 20260707, plus Norton Rose Fulbright, Baker McKenzie, WilmerHale, Foley and Lardner, the National Law Review and Holland and Knight.

snippet.title: CANParks Is Here! Introducing Canada’s Homegrown Ham Radio Parks Program 🇨🇦
snippet.description:
Hi everyone, Stuart, VE9CF here — and I’d like to introduce you to CANParks, Canada’s Ham Radio Parks Program.

Register for CANParks here - https://canparks.ca

CANParks was created by Canadian amateur radio operators for people who enjoy portable operating, chasing parks and exploring the incredible outdoor spaces found across our country.

Our philosophy is simple: A Park Is A Park. If it is a recognized Canadian park, open to the general public, and the proper name contains the word Park or Parc, it may qualify for the CANParks program. That includes national, provincial, territorial, municipal and community parks.

Activating is simple. You and your station must be at the park, and just one valid amateur radio contact is required. HF, VHF, UHF, repeaters, satellites, voice, CW and digital modes are all welcome. A practical 250-metre allowance also helps operators stay safe when operating from a parking area serving the park.

CANParks can accept eligible CANParks, POTA and WWFF ADIF logs, and members can recommend new parks directly through their CANParks account.

Most importantly, CANParks belongs to its members. Canadian operators have a voice in how the program develops, which parks are included and what features are built next.

Visit canparks.ca, create your free account, explore the park directory and join us in bringing Canadian parks to the amateur radio world.

I’m Stuart, VE9CF. Thanks for watching — and I hope to hear you from a CANParks park soon.

#hamradio #canada #amateurradio

snippet.title: What Happened to Ham Radio? It's Not What You Think
snippet.description:
Free Video Course - The Top 5 Beginner Ham Radio Frustrations (and How To Overcome Them): https://hamradiolaunchpad.com/free

----

FREE PDF — every number and chart in this video, with the source for each: https://hamradiolaunchpad.com/license-data/

----

I got my Technician license in 2010 and then barely used it for a
decade. When I finally went and pulled the numbers on this hobby,
I found out I wasn't unusual — I was the pattern.

There are 48,000 fewer licensed hams in the US than there were five
years ago, and that number has dropped every six months for five
years straight. Over the same stretch, the number of POTA activations 
went up 400%.

Both are true. Both come from public data, and all of it is linked
below.

This is what the FCC numbers actually show about where ham radio
went, which part of it is shrinking, which part is growing, and the
one change that would fix the biggest gap between them.

----

THE DATA BEHIND THIS VIDEO (free PDF download)

Thirteen pages: the FCC license file, ARRL counts, POTA's own dashboard, Field Day results, and a direct link to every one. Includes the license-class breakdown the headline number hides, and three widely-quoted figures I left out on purpose and what's wrong with each: https://hamradiolaunchpad.com/license-data/

----

SOURCES — every number in this video:

US license counts, historical series (1997–2026)
Keith Greiner, AmateurRadioData — primary source is the FCC license file:
https://sites.google.com/site/amateurradiodata/home

Current US license counts by class
ARRL FCC License Counts:
http://www.arrl.org/fcc-license-counts

New license applications by year (2019: 30,078 · 2025: 25,943)
FCC Universal Licensing System, Application Search (Purpose = New · Type = Individual · full calendar year):
https://wireless2.fcc.gov/UlsApp/ApplicationSearch/searchAmateur.jsp

Parks on the Air statistics by year
Official POTA statistics dashboard:
https://stats.pota.ninja

POTA activator license classes (57% Extra / 39% General / 2% Technician)
Frank Howell K4FMH, January 2026:
https://k4fmh.com/2026/01/26/a-snapshot-of-u-s-pota-sites-activators-and-activations/

2025 ARRL Field Day results — participants, entries, QSOs by mode
QST, December 2025:
https://contests.arrl.org/ContestResults/2025/Field-Day-2025-FinalQSTResults.pdf

FT8 overtaking voice and CW in 2017 (Club Log data)
ARRL:
https://www.arrl.org/news/mode-usage-evaluation-2017-was-the-year-when-digital-modes-changed-forever

FCC application fee — and the upgrade exemption
ARRL:
http://www.arrl.org/fcc-application-fee

QRP Labs assembled kit waiting list:
https://www.qrp-labs.com/qcxmini/assembled.html

Morse code testing eliminated, February 2007
ARRL:
http://www.arrl.org/ham-radio-licenses

----

Chapters:
00:00 - Is ham radio dying?
01:45 - The numbers, and where they dropped
03:06 - Why nobody's walking in the front door
03:51 - This has happened twice before
05:10 - What the internet actually took

07:15 - The gear went portable
07:50 - Where people are taking it
08:40 - Who's actually out there
09:50 - The most fixable problem in ham radio
10:34 - So is it dying?

----

snippet.title: What Can You ACTUALLY Do With the A-General Engineering License in California + Full Updated Exam!
snippet.description:
Complete Course:
https://digitalconstructive.com/generalA

Full list of jobs you can do with the A-General Engineering license: https://digitalconstructive.com/generala-license-jobs/



Content of the Examination
The General Engineering (A) Examination is
divided into eight major sections:

1. Planning and Estimating (15%)

• Reviewing plans and specifications
• Code compliance
• Evaluating job sites
• Coordinating projects with other trades
• Estimating costs for materials, equipment,
and labor

2. Structural Principles (6%)

• Constructing structures
• Seismic requirements
• Basic engineering

3. Earthwork and Surveying (15%)

• Surveying job sites
• Preparing job sites
• Assessing soil conditions
• Assessing soil compaction and expansion

4. Subsurface, Surface, and
Elevated Piping Work (21%)

• Shoring and sloping excavations
• Preventing erosion
• Tunneling, drilling, and boring
• Installing pipelines
• Connecting and testing systems
• Connecting dry utilities

5. Foundation and Concrete Construction (11%)

• Constructing forms and falsework
• Placing and finishing concrete
• Installing pilings and foundations

6. Buildings, Structures, and Related Work (9%)

• Installing mechanical systems
• Installing plumbing pipes
• Installing electrical systems
• Demolition, disposal, and recycling

7. Roadwork and Paving (5%)

• Base for highways, roads, and parking lots

8. Safety (18%)
• Personnel and job site safety
• Personal protective equipment (PPE)
• Hazardous material safety

Sample Questions

Below are three typical examination questions.
The correct answer is marked with an asterisk (*).

1. What type of connection is used to flush a
water line?

a. An air release valve
b. A blow-off valve*
c. A post indicator valve
d. A detector check valve

2. What is the MOST important reason for
someone to supervise the rate of pour when
concrete is used for high wall forms?

a. To prevent rebar movement
b. To ensure proper vibration
c. To avoid cement pockets
d. To avoid collapse*

3. Excluding any shrinkage or compaction,
approximately how much backfill material is
required to fill the void after removing a 10,000-
gallon rectangular underground tank at surface
level?

a. 30 cu. yds.
b. 40 cu. yds.
c. 50 cu. yds.*
d. 60 cu. yds.

*All questions are written and reviewed by licensed
contractors who are actively working in the trade*

お天気の状況、時間帯によって混雑具合がことなります

都市部の公園ですので、運用には十分お気をつけください
